chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from some of his companions who said:
Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) was asked: 'Do the people have the leeway to abandon asking about what they are in need of?' So he said: 'No.'

key_terms.الْمَسْأَلَة: The questioning/asking (seeking answers to religious matters one needs to know)
key_terms.يَحْتَاجُونَ: They are in need of (those things which are religiously necessary for them to know)
key_terms.يَسَعُ: Has leeway/is permissible (used in classical fiqh to indicate latitude or exemption from an obligation)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for Muslims to neglect asking about religious matters they need?
ai.summary: Imam Ali al-Ridha (peace be upon him) was asked whether it is permissible for people to neglect seeking answers to their religious questions. He gave a decisive one-word reply: 'No.' This ruling reinforces that seeking religious knowledge to fulfill one's obligations is not optional — the community cannot excuse itself from inquiry. In the context of early Shia scholarship, this hadith addressed communities with limited access to the Imam, emphasizing the continuing duty to seek answers through available channels.
